title: What are Bridging Loans and How Do They Work?
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Its SEO/result title is confirmed as "What are Bridging Loans and How Do They Work?". The exact-URL search [a] returned no Silver Oak result at all (only third-party guides, ignored). The site: search [b] returned the page plus eight sibling Silver Oak bridging pages, and the search tool's summary blended them, attributing points to "one article" / "another" without naming which. Thesis as summarised: a bridging loan is a short-term loan used to "bridge the gap" between a future cash flow and a current expense; the most common use is buying a new home before selling the current one, with the existing property serving as security and the loan repaid from the proceeds of sale once the old property is sold; terms quoted as between 1 and 36 months (one article) or usually 6 to 24 months (another); lenders focus mainly on the property's value and the borrower's exit plan and set a loan-to-value (LTV) ratio; interest is either rolled up and settled at the end of the term or serviced (paid regularly); rates are higher than a standard mortgage ("double, if not triple"), and arrangement and valuation fees add to the total. No lender names, current rates, eligibility criteria, FAQ blocks, calls to action, H1 or meta description were revealed for this page.
